summary: Woncheol Yun works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woosung Huh specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

Wu Hung is an art historian and sinologist who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard University (PhD ~1980–1987). His posts include Harvard (1990), the University of Chicago (since 1994), and Oxford (2015–2016).
Wulstan Fletcher is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Xianda works in Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from The University of Hong Kong (attested 2016), studying under K. L. Dhammajoti and Toshiichi Endo.

Xiangguang Zhou worked in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Swami Sivananda Saraswati. He held posts at the University of Allahabad, University of Delhi, LBSNAA, and served as Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tsinghua and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. He held major posts at Peking University (1946, 1978, 1980) and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Xiaoling Wu was a scholar of sinology and Indology. He held appointments at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1949), Peking University (~1949–1952), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoting Wei is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Kathy Ku Cheng Mei (attested 2004).

Xinchuan Huang was a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1954–1958). He held research appointments at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from approximately 1979 until 2021.

Xinru Liu specializes in history, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher (~1980–1985) and held posts at CASS (1993) and The College of New Jersey (~1999).
Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xu Dishan was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford. He held posts at Peking University (~1926–1935), Tsinghua University (~1928–1930), and The University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xuesong Zhang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. He served as a Research Associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017) and Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011).

Y. Karunadasa is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Peradeniya and the University of London under David Friedman. He held posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Hong Kong.

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University, completing doctoral research under Gregory Schopen, and later taught in Hebrew University's Indian Studies Department (attested 2000).
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and sinology. She earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

Yang Renshan was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), the Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and the Buddhist Research Society (1910), which he headed in 1910.
Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ven. Hojin and earned his D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1998 under Richard Gombrich.
